author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Archdiocese of Detroit issues advisory on group calling itself The National Catholic Church
text:
The Archdiocese of Detroit Department of Communications announced on May 27 that parishes are invited to publish an advisory concerning a group known as “The National Catholic Church,” which operates in Dearborn and other locations. The advisory states that while the group claims to offer “traditional sacraments” and openly acknowledges it is not in communion with Rome, its use of the term “Catholic” may cause confusion among members of the faithful regarding its relationship to the Catholic Church.
According to the Archdiocese, The National Catholic Church appears affiliated with The Society of Our Lady, Queen of all Saints. This organization has previously been identified by the Archdiocese as not being in ecclesiastical communion with the Roman Catholic Church. The statement reads: “In the interest of truth and to avoid confusion among the faithful, we must clarify that, as best we are able to determine, The National Catholic Church and The Society of Our Lady, Queen of all Saints are not organizations in ecclesiastical communion with the Catholic Church. Catholics are advised to avoid association with these groups.”
The communication emphasizes each member’s responsibility within the faith community “to reduce error, avoid schism, and promote ecclesiastical communion.” It concludes by encouraging prayer for unity: “Let us pray that God will bring all Christian communities into full communion with the Roman Catholic Church, so that we may all be one. (cf. John 17:21)”
The Archdiocese manages more than 200 parishes and supports initiatives related to marriage, family life, youth programs, and social justice efforts through charitable organizations such as Catholic Charities, and advances Gospel-centered activities across southeastern Michigan counties including Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, St. Clair, Lapeer, and Monroe, according to its official website .
